service.description: Whether the user may see a request in Projects (as get#RecordLinkInfo has it) and triage it (canTriage: one who may work in its project, ironstone.projects.ProjectServices.get#ProjectAccess canUpdate; for a request with no project a Projects team member or manager), with the user's part in it (isRaiser, isAssignee, isParty). need: check answers without an error; view adds "not available" when it is not seen; triage adds an error when the user may not triage it.

The rows of Requests (design-projects.md §6): the requests of the projects the user sees, and those with no project of the types the user's organizations triage, in one list, narrowed by the find, sorted and paged, each decorated, with the count of each list (without the find). The lists: new (Submitted with no assignee; the managers' default), assigned (open, the user the Assignee; the team's default), review (Submitted), accepted (Reviewed), progress (In Progress), mine (filed by the user, or the user its Reporter; open), closed (Completed or Cancelled, the latest first) and all. rootWorkEffortId fixes a project (ProjectDetail's Requests tab); unassigned narrows to the requests with no project. A status in the find takes the place of the list's.

Requests as Requests and its board show them: the link, the type, the status (label and color), the project, the customer and assignee (names; another user's personal contact by its id), the priority, the due date, the channel (app, email or form), the work (done of the total linked work items) and when it was updated. roleMap (requestId|roleTypeId to partyId) when the caller has it.

NewRequest (design-projects.md §6): a Submitted request filed by the user, in a project the user may work in (or with none, for triage), with its type (the project's default when not given), customer, name, description, priority, due and assignee (empty: unassigned, for triage; the project's triage assignee when it has one).

One triage change of a request, by one who may triage it (get#ProjectRequestAccess): action status (value the status: Reviewed is Accept, In Progress Start, Completed with resolutionEnumId, by default Fixed for a bug and else Completed, Cancelled with resolutionEnumId Rejected or Duplicate, Submitted puts an In Progress one back), assign (value a party; empty unassigns), project (value a project the user may work in; empty takes it off), priority (1 to 9), due (yyyy-MM-dd, empty for none), type (a RequestType). With comment (Complete and Cancel), the text goes on the request's conversation as a note. A draft is the requester's: Submit is in Commons.

RequestBulk (design-projects.md §6): one triage change on each selected request (requestIds, a comma list): assign, project, priority, accept, start, cancel (value the resolution), makeWork (a work item of each in its project) or linkWork (value a work item's key). Each request in a transaction of its own; the ones that fail are counted and named, the others done.

RequestHeader (design-projects.md §6): the request's name, type, priority, customer, project, assignee, due and description, by one who may triage it. Only the fields given change; an empty assignee or project leaves them as they are (Assign and Set project take them off).

MakeWorkItem (design-projects.md §6): a work item of the request in a project the user may work in (the request's, or the one given; one with no project takes it), through mantle.request.RequestServices make#RequestWorkItem; the request is accepted once it has work. Defaults from the request: title, type, priority, due, description.

LinkWorkItem (design-projects.md §6): an existing work item (by its key) is the request's work (RequestWorkEffort), for one who may triage the request and see the item; a request with no project takes the item's. Linking again changes nothing.
Takes a work item off the request's work (the item stays), for one who may triage the request.

actions.script: ec.service.sync().name('ironstone.projects.ProjectRequestServices.get#ProjectRequestAccess').parameters({requestId: requestId, need: 'triage'}).call() if (ec.message.hasError()) return // an item the user may not see is not taken off, and not told of (HiddenItems.js mayName); a link to an item that is gone is if (ec.entity.find('mantle.work.effort.WorkEffort').condition('workEffortId', workEffortId).disableAuthz().count() > 0 && !ec.resource.script('component://mr-boss/service/ironstone/projects/HiddenItems.js').mayName(workEffortId)) { ec.message.addError(ec.resource.expand('${id} is not a work item of the request', '', {id: workEffortId})); return } ec.entity.find('mantle.request.RequestWorkEffort').condition('requestId', requestId).condition('workEffortId', workEffortId).deleteAll() message = ec.resource.expand('${id} taken off the request', '', {id: workEffortId})

service.description: ConvertToProject (design-projects.md §6): a new project from the request (its key and name; the name and description from the request, its customer the client), for the Projects managers (create#QuickProject); the request is the new project's, In Progress (mantle.request.RequestServices.convert#RequestToProject).

What RequestDetail shows in Projects (design-projects.md §6, on Commons' get#RequestDetail for the record, its people and linked records): the triage the user may do (canTriage), the status-bar's moves (Accept, Start, Complete, Cancel, back to Submitted, Re-open), the facts (customer, project, priority, due, assignee, filed by, date, channel), the work (its linked work items decorated as WorkItems shows them, with the done count), the items (RequestItem rows, for purchase, quote and inventory requests or when it has some), whether the customer is outside the organization (Chatter opens on Send message), and the options of the dialogs.
The work items a request may be linked to: by key or title, of the projects the user sees (of the request's project first when it has one), as drop-down options.

A project's intake (design-projects.md §4 ProjectRequests' Intake box and ProjectSettings' Intake box), for one who sees the project: its intake account (the mail account and plus tag that file mail into it, and the address they make), its email rules (the createRequest and createWorkItem rules naming the project, of the accounts the user may change), the public form's link (formPath /r/<token>, empty when off), the triage assignee and the default request type; canManage for the changes.

ProjectSettings' Intake box, by one who manages the project: the mail account (one the user may manage) and its plus tag (letters, digits, dot, dash), which also write the project's email rule (save#IntakeAddress: mail to the address makes requests, or work items for internal senders), the triage assignee and the default request type. formOn Y makes the public form's link when there is none; N turns it off.
The public form's link of a project, by one who manages it: rotate (a new link; the old one stops working) or off (no link).

An intake address (design-projects.md §12 EmailIntake): the project's mail account and plus tag (WstIntakeAccount, WstIntakePlusTag), and the email rule on the account that makes them: To contains the address (local+tag@domain, or the account's address with no tag), the action createRequest (or createWorkItem: work items for internal senders) with the project as its value, written as the user (org.moqui.mail.EmailClientServices create#EmailRule or update#EmailRule, so the user must manage the account). An empty account takes the address off: the settings, and the user's rules naming the project. For one who manages the project.

IntakeSettings (design-projects.md §12): the organization's request types offered and triaged with no project, the default type and the default triage assignee (PartySetting ProjIntake), the request categories, the intake addresses (each project's account, plus tag and rule, of the projects the user sees), the public form settings (ProjPublicForm) and the mail accounts the user may manage.

IntakeSettings' IntakeTypes, for the Projects managers: the request types offered (on the form and new requests), those Projects triages with no project, the default type and the default triage assignee, as the organization's PartySetting ProjIntake (short keys within its 255 characters, impl-projects.md F9).

IntakeSettings' PublicForm, for the Projects managers: the CAPTCHA on (it needs the reCAPTCHA keys of the reCAPTCHA.site.key and reCAPTCHA.secret.key preferences), files taken, at most how many and how large each (MB), and whether a confirmation email goes from the project's intake account, as PartySetting ProjPublicForm.

IntakeSettings' RequestCategories, for the Projects managers: a category (requestCategoryId for an existing one) with its description, parent (not itself or below it) and responsible party; remove deletes one no request uses (remove).
